main_turf.bias_notes: Clockwise (right-handed). Forbes is a well-maintained 1,600m regional country oval with a 350m home straight and starting chutes for 1100m, 1300m, and 1600m races. Short home-stretch run-ins favor horses settling on or near the pace on firm ground, while broad sweeping bends allow fair racing across middle distances.
main_turf.post_bias: In 1100m and 1200m sprint events, inside barriers (1–4) hold a distinct advantage into the quick first turn. In 1300m and 1600m route races, the chute run allows wider draws (5–9) time to find a good running position. On heavy/wet tracks, jockey bias shifts wide towards the middle of the track on the home turn.

handicapping_angles.nsw_country_and_provincial_shippers: Forbes attracts premier NSW Country and Sydney/Provincial stables (Brett Robb, Gayna Williams, Clint Lundholm, Bjorn Baker, Brett Cavanough). Heavily upgrade horses dropping down from Sydney Metro, Dubbo, or Wellington into NSW Country Benchmark (BM58-BM74) or Maiden company.
handicapping_angles.short_350m_straight_pace_advantage: On Good 4 / Soft 5 surfaces, prominent pressers ('P') and front-runners ('E') controlling the tempo into the 350m home stretch are difficult to run down. Avoid deep back-markers unless early pace fractions are severely contested.
handicapping_angles.forbes_cup_metro_class_translation: During the iconic Forbes Cup Showcase meeting in August, racing quality elevates toward Provincial/Metro Showcase grade. Horses performing well here during showcase cards should be treated as higher-tier contenders.
handicapping_angles.nsw_benchmark_weight_penalty: In NSW Country Benchmark handicaps, top-weighted runners carrying 60kg+ face a strict burden. Value fit, well-weighted drop-downs or skilled claiming apprentices taking weight off top-rated contenders.
